text:
jamal: heads up — since ~02:00 UTC we're seeing a spike of Pending pods w/ FitFailure on nodepool g2-high, ~120 pods, mostly small-batch inference jobs. looks like binpacking fragmentation again :grimace:
anya: ugh. any error lines from scheduler?
jamal: scheduler: "failed to fit pod" -> reasons: InsufficientNvidiaGPU and NoNodesAvailable. pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25` (we used fractional to express tiny bursts)
kevin: wait we're still requesting fractional GPUs? k8s device plugin doesn't support fractional natively unless MIG is used — which pool is that on?
ria: g2-high is mixed: some nodes MIG-enabled (A100-7g), but most are vanilla A100-40g. autoscaler has been spinning up new 40g nodes to satisfy one 7g partition cause mismatch.
jamal: autoscaler log: "scaleUp: triggered for 3 nodes, reason: 120 pending pods" — but the new nodes are 40g and no MIG partitions so scheduler still can't place 0.25 requests.
anya: ops-bot reported last night we drained some MIG nodes for kernel patching. maybe we lost partitioned capacity.
ops-bot: [autoscaler] scaled up 3 nodes in pool g2-high at 02:14 UTC; [node-maint] drained 2 nodes in pool g2-mig for kernel-5.15 patch at 01:50 UTC.
kevin: root cause seems to be fractional request + mixed node flavors + maintenance removing MIG partitions -> fragmentation. proposals: 1) change pod requests to `nvidia.com/mig-cores: 1` where applicable, 2) add a schedule rule to prefer MIG-enabled nodes, or 3) use a tiny-node pool with MIG=7g nodes only.
ria: agree. quick mitigation: add nodeAffinity to place small-batch pods on the g2-mig pool that still has partitions. also temporarily allow toleration to schedule onto 40g by switching request to `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` for fallback (costly).
anya: can we alter the cluster-autoscaler config to prefer adding g2-mig nodes instead of 40g? right now it uses cheapest-zone first.
kevin: yes we can set expander: priority and set priorities such that g2-mig pool ranks higher for those pod labels. also CA's `balancing` heuristics might be causing extra nodes.
jamal: created a quick patch to the deployment template to add nodeSelector: `kubernetes.azure.com/pool: g2-mig` for the small-batch app. rolling it now.
ria: also opened a ticket to ops to revert the MIG maintenance schedule or stagger it — losing partitioned nodes at scale is risky.
ops-bot: [ticket] #INFRA-982: 'Reconsider kernel patch window for g2-mig to avoid concurrent partition loss' created by ria at 02:28 UTC.
kevin: longer term we should stop using fractional GPUs as a request unit. either use MIG explicit resources or add a sidecar that batches locally to reduce scheduling pressure. batching reduces token cost anyway.
anya: +1 on batching. also request we add a probe that alerts when >30 pending FitFailure because it's a recurring pattern.
jamal: state after nodeSelector change: pending count dropped from 120 -> 6 in 7m, autoscaler still cleaning up extra nodes. will follow up with a postmortem.
ria: thanks — can you paste the CA plan change PR when ready?
jamal: will do. TL;DR: fragmentation + maintenance + fractional requests -> chaotic scale-up. mitigation: nodeAffinity -> g2-mig, CA expander tweak, and prod follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
